note: Event cards typed by Orbis from the cited Wikipedia articles. Dates are Gregorian; cards marked Julian show the Julian date their sources use (England kept the Julian calendar until 1752).

items.title: Vicky marries into Prussia
items.text: Victoria's eldest daughter married Prince Frederick of Prussia. Their son Wilhelm, born in 1859, was Victoria's first grandchild and became German Emperor in 1888.

items.title: Alexandra marries the Prince of Wales
items.text: Christian IX's eldest daughter Alexandra married Victoria's son, the future Edward VII. Their son became George V.

items.title: Dagmar marries the Russian heir
items.text: Christian IX's daughter Dagmar married the future Alexander III of Russia and took the name Maria Feodorovna. Their son became Nicholas II.

items.title: Alix of Hesse becomes empress
items.text: Victoria's granddaughter Alix of Hesse married Nicholas II weeks after he became emperor. She passed the haemophilia she carried from Victoria to their son Alexei.

items.title: Victoria dies
items.text: Queen Victoria died at Osborne House on the Isle of Wight. Her grandson Wilhelm II was at her bedside.
items.source: Wikipedia, 'Death and state funeral of Queen Victoria'

items.title: Ena becomes queen of Spain
items.text: Victoria's granddaughter Victoria Eugenie of Battenberg married Alfonso XIII. On the way back from the wedding an anarchist threw a bomb at the royal carriage; the couple survived, but people in the crowd were killed.

items.title: Nine kings at one funeral
items.text: Nine reigning kings followed Edward VII's coffin through London, among them George V, Wilhelm II, Haakon VII and George I of Greece: most were his relatives.
items.source: Wikipedia, 'Death and state funeral of Edward VII'

items.title: The Willy-Nicky telegrams
items.text: Between 29 July and 1 August 1914 Wilhelm II and Nicholas II exchanged ten telegrams in English, signed 'Willy' and 'Nicky', trying and failing to stop the war.

items.title: Nicholas II abdicates
items.text: Facing revolution in Petrograd, Nicholas II abdicated in his train at Pskov. On 17 July 1918 the Bolsheviks shot him, Alexandra and their five children at Yekaterinburg.

items.title: Windsor
items.text: With Britain at war with Germany, George V dropped the German name Saxe-Coburg and Gotha and named his house after Windsor Castle.

items.title: Wilhelm II flees to the Netherlands
items.text: With Germany defeated and revolution in Berlin, Wilhelm II crossed into the neutral Netherlands. He abdicated formally on 28 November and lived at Doorn until 1941.
